title: Lab summary – diabetes management from clinical cases (English)
html:
Source: LAB summary practical.pdf – 7 pages

Complete Guide to Diabetes Management - Based on Clinical Cases #1

  • 1. DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR DIABETES
  • ● Diabetes diagnosis is confirmed by ANY of the following:
  • ☆ Fasting venous glucose ≥ 126 mg/dL (no caloric intake for ≥8 hours)
  • ☆ 2-hour glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL during OGTT (75g glucose load)
  • ☆ HbA1c ≥ 6.5%
  • ☆ Random venous glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL in a patient w/ classic symptoms (polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss)
  • Note: In symptomatic patients with glucose ≥200 mg/dL, HbA1c or OGTT are NOT required for diagnosis
  • ● Prediabetes Criteria:
  • ☆ Impaired Fasting Glucose (IFG): Fasting glucose 110-125 mg/dL
  • ☆ Impaired Glucose Tolerance (IGT): 2-hour OGTT 140-199 mg/dL
  • ☆ HbA1c: 5.7-6.4%
  • ● Gestational Diabetes (GDM) - 75g OGTT Criteria:
  • GDM diagnosed if ANY value equals or exceeds threshold
  • 2. DIABETES CLASSIFICATION
  • MODY (Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young):
  • ☆ Age <25 years
  • ☆ Family history of diabetes in multiple generations
  • ☆ Non-obese (BMI normal)
  • ☆ Absence of autoantibodies (ddx DMT1)
  • ☆ Preserved C-peptide (ddx DMT1)
  • ☆ Genetic testing required for confirmation
  • 3. COMPLETE INITIAL ASSESSMENT (Additional Investigations)
  • ● For ALL Newly Diagnosed Diabetes:
  • ☆ HbA1c (if not already done)
  • ☆ Fasting glucose (repeat for confirmation if needed)
  • ☆ Urinalysis (glucose, ketones, protein)
  • ☆ Renal function (creatinine, eGFR)
  • ☆ Liver function tests (ALT, AST)
  • ☆ Lipid profile (total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides)
  • ● For DMT2– Screening for chronic complications (at diagnosis vs. 5y after dg in DMT1):
  • ○ Diabetic RETINOPATHY - fundus examination ; ○ Diabetic NEPHROPATHY - urine ACR, eGFR
  • ○ Diabetic NEUROPATHY - foot examination, monofilament, vibration ; ○ Cardiovascular disease - ECG, ABI

● For Diabetic Neuropathy assessment: #2

  • ○ Foot inspection - skin appearance, temperature, interdigital spaces
  • ○ Pulse palpation (dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial) ; ○ Reflex testing (ankle reflex)
  • ○ Monofilament test (pressure sensitivity)
  • ○ Vibration test: Tuning fork on bony proeminence of tip of halux, "tell me when you don’t feel vibration anymore", read the
  • number you see (NV= 6-8<60y or 4-8>60y)
  • ○ Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) - Normal 0.9-1.3
  • 4. THERAPEUTIC OBJECTIVES
  • ● Glycemic Targets:
  • Elderly/Frail Patients (Case No. 9):
  • ☆ Preprandial: 100-140 mg/dL
  • ☆ Postprandial: < 200 mg/dL
  • ● Weight Goals:
  • ☆ Weight loss: 5-10% over 3-6 months for overweight/obese pt
  • ☆ GDM: Keep weight gain w/in guidelines (max 3kg until delivery)
  • ● BP Targets— General: < 140/90 mmHg ; High CV risk / Diabetes w/ complications: < 130/80 mmHg
  • ● Lipid Targets (Based on CV Risk):
  • <-
  • 5. TREATMENT STRATEGIES
  • Lifestyle optimisation + pharmaco tx
  • A. Lifestyle Optimization - 7 Components =>
  • B. Pharmacological Treatment :
  • ☆ Metformin initiation:
  • Start: 500 mg BID for 1 week
  • Increase to: 1000 mg BID (2 g/day total)
  • Monitor: GI tolerance, renal function
  • ☆ Insulin Initiation (Basal):
  • Starting dose: 0.1-0.2 IU/kg/d (or 10 IU/d)
  • Titration: Adjust by +2 IU every 3-7 days based on fasting glucose
  • Target fasting glucose: 80-130 mg/dL❤️
  • ☆ Rapid-Acting Insulin:
  • Admin: Before meals (1-3 times/d)
  • Adjust: +2 IU for postprandial hyperglycemia (>180 mg/dL)
  • Reduce: -2 IU for postprandial hypoglycemia or if pre-meal glucose <70 mg/dL

● DKA/HHS Treatment (Emergency): #3

  • 1. Rehydration:
  • ▪ Maintain K⁺ =4-5 mEq/L with KCl supplementation
  • ▪ When glucose <250 mg/dL=> Switch to Glucose 10% + insulin
  • 2. Insulin Therapy:
  • ○ Bolus: 0.1 IU/kg IV rapid insulin then ○ Continuous: 0.1 IU/kg/hour IV
  • Monitor glucose hourly and transition to SC insulin when:
  • pH ≥7.3, Bicarbonate ≥18, ketones cleared & patient eating
  • 3. Bicarbonate (DKA only):
  • Give if pH < 7.0: 100 ml of 8.4% bicarbonate (⚠️ Do NOT give if pH ≥ 7.0)
  • C. Antidiabetic Agents - indications:
  • D. Insulin Administration Guidelines:
  • ● Injection Sites:
  • ☆ Basal insulin => Thigh/Abdomen
  • ☆ Rapid Acting => Abdomen (≥2 cm from
  • navel, within 10 cm radius)
  • ☆ Premixed => Thigh/Abdomen
  • ⚠️ Rotate sites to prevent lipohypertrophy!
  • ● Insulin Regimens:
  • ☆ Basal-only: 1-2 injections/day (DMT2)
  • ☆ Basal-bolus: Basal (1-2x/d) + Rapid-acting
  • (before meals) - DMT1
  • ☆ Premixed: 2-3 times/d, before meals
  • 6. MONITORING PLAN
  • ● Self-Monitoring of
  • Blood Glucose (SMBG):
  • ● 7-Point Glycemic Profile:
  • 1. Fasting
  • 2. Post-breakfast (2h)
  • 3. Pre-lunch
  • 4. Post-lunch (2h)
  • 5. Pre-dinner
  • 6. Post-dinner (2h)
  • 7. Bedtime
  • ● Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM):
  • - TIR (Time In Range): >70% (70-180 mg/dL)
  • - TBR (Time Below Range): <4% (<70 mg/dL)
  • - CV (Coefficient of Variation): ≤36%
  • - GMI (Glucose Management Indicator): <7%
  • ● Lab monitoring:
  • 7. COMPLICATION SCREENING
  • ☆ Diabetic Neuropathy - RF:
  • - Age
  • - Duration of diabetes
  • - Poor glycemic control
  • - Poor lipid control
  • - HTN
  • - Smoking

☆ Diabetic Nephropathy (KDIGO Staging): #4

  • - G1: eGFR ≥90
  • - G2: eGFR 60-89
  • - G3a: eGFR 45-59
  • - G3b: eGFR 30-44
  • - G4: eGFR 15-29
  • - G5: eGFR <15
  • - A1: ACR <30 mg/g
  • - A2: ACR 30-300 mg/g
  • - A3: ACR >300 mg/g
  • Foot Examination Components:
  • Skin: Appearance, color, temperature, interdigital spaces
  • Pulses: Dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial
  • Reflexes: Ankle reflex
  • Sensation: Monofilament (pressure), 128Hz tuning fork (vibration)
  • ABI: Normal = >0.9; <0.9 suggests PAD; <0.5 suggests severe PAD
  • 8. INSULIN ADJUSTMENT ALGORITHM
  • Step 1: Identify the problem
  • Step 2: Consider lifestyle factors
  • ▪ Physical activity → May require dose reduction
  • ▪ Carbohydrate intake → Match insulin to carbs
  • ▪ Alcohol consumption → Can cause delayed hypoglycemia
  • ▪ Illness/Infection → May require dose increase
  • ▪ Weight changes → May require dose adjustment
  • Step 3: Rule of 1800/1500
  • For rapid-acting insulin: 1800 ÷ total daily dose = glucose drop per 1 IU
  • For regular insulin: 1500 ÷ total daily dose = glucose drop per 1 IU
  • Step 4: Correction Factor
  • Start: Reduce by 2 IU per adjustment
  • Minimum interval: 3-7 days between adjustments (unless acute)
  • Monitor: 3-7 days post-adjustment to assess effect
  • FIX EMERGENCY FIRST (hypogly <70), THEN BASAL (80-130), then RAPID ACTING (PP<180)

9. KEY MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES BY CASE TYPE #5

  • Newly Diagnosed DMT1 (with Ketones):
  • URGENT: Check pH and bicarbonate
  • Immediate: Hospitalization for DKA management
  • Stabilization: IV fluids + insulin
  • Transition: From IV to SC insulin when pH ≥7.3
  • Education: Insulin technique, SMBG, sick-day rules
  • Follow-up: C-peptide, autoantibodies
  • Newly Diagnosed DMT2:
  • Lifestyle: Intensive lifestyle modification
  • Pharmacology: Metformin first-line
  • Complication screening: Full assessment
  • Cardiovascular risk assessment: SCORE2/SCORE2-OP
  • Consider: GLP-1 RA or SGLT2i if ASCVD/HF/CKD
  • Established DMT2 - Uncontrolled:
  • Step 1: Optimize lifestyle
  • Step 2: Titrate current medications
  • Step 3: Add new agents (in order of benefit):
  • - ASCVD: GLP-1 RA or SGLT2i
  • - CKD: SGLT2i
  • - HF: SGLT2i
  • - Obesity: GLP-1 RA
  • Need to avoid hypoglycemia: DPP-4i
  • Step 4: Consider insulin if HbA1c >9% despite OADs
  • GDM:
  • Lifestyle: First-line treatment
  • Insulin: If lifestyle insufficient (Tresiba for fasting; rapid-acting for post-meals)
  • Insulin adjustments: +2 IU for fasting >95 mg/dL
  • Monitoring: 7-day SMBG profile; weekly at clinic
  • Postpartum: Discontinue insulin immediately; monitor fasting glucose for 1 day
  • Long-term: Screen every 1-3 years (50% risk of T2D within 10 years)
  • 10. DYSLIPIDEMIA MANAGEMENT
  • ● Cardiovascular Risk Assessment:
  • SCORE2: For individuals <70 years
  • SCORE2-OP: For individuals ≥70 years
  • SCORE2-D: For individuals with DMT2
  • ● Very High CV Risk = LDL Goal <55 mg/dL AND ≥50% Reduction
  • Examples: ASCVD (MI, stroke, PAD); DMT2 + target organ damage (nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy) ; SCORE2 ≥10%;
  • Severe CKD (eGFR <30)
  • ● High CV Risk = LDL Goal <70 mg/dL
  • Examples: DMT2 + one risk factor ; SCORE2 5-10%; Moderate CKD (eGFR 30-59)

● Treatment Approach: #6

  • ☆ Statins: First-line (Atorvastatin, Rosuvastatin - 40-80mg)
  • +/- Ezetimibe: Add if statin alone insufficient
  • +/- PCSK9 inhibitors: Add if still not at goal (Alirocumab, Evolocumab)
  • ▪ Inclisiran: Alternative in very high risk
  • ▪ Fenofibrate: For severe hypertriglyceridemia (TG ≥500 mg/dL) - risk of pancreatitis
  • ▪ Fibrates: For TG >200 mg/dL despite statin
  • ● Severe Hypertriglyceridemia (TG >500 mg/dL):
  • Primary goal: Prevent pancreatitis → Reduce TG
  • Treatment: Fenofibrate + Omega-3
  • Secondary goal: LDL target
  • 11. SPECIAL POPULATIONS
  • ○ Elderly Patients:
  • Less stringent glycemic targets: Fasting 100-140 mg/dL
  • Consider: Cognitive impairment, polypharmacy, falls risk
  • ⚠️Avoid: Sulfonylureas, aggressive insulin titration
  • Preferred: DPP-4 inhibitors, basal insulin
  • ○ Professional Drivers:
  • ⚠️Avoid: Medications causing hypoglycemia (sulfonylureas)
  • Preferred: SGLT2i, DPP-4i, GLP-1 RA
  • If insulin: Must be able to monitor glucose regularly
  • Safety: Driving restrictions for recurrent hypoglycemia
  • 12. KEY EDUCATIONAL POINTS FOR PATIENTS
  • ● Insulin Injection Technique:
  • ▪ Select site (abdomen for rapid, thigh for basal)
  • ▪ Clean skin with alcohol swab
  • ▪ Pinch skin (if thin patient)
  • ▪ Insert needle at 90° (or 45° if thin)
  • ▪ Inject slowly and steadily
  • ▪ Hold for 5-10 seconds
  • ▪ Remove needle and discard safely
  • ▪ Rotate sites to prevent lipohypertrophy
  • ● Sick Day Rules:
  • Never stop insulin (even if not eating)
  • Check glucose every 2-4 hours
  • Check ketones if glucose >250 mg/dL
  • Stay hydrated (small sips frequently)
  • Call doctor if:
  • - Vomiting >2 hours;
  • - Glucose >300 despite extra insulin;
  • - Moderate-large ketones;
  • - Confusion/altered mental status
  • ● Insulin reading: Insert the strip, wait until the device turns on, THEN put the blood on your finger and then dip the strip on
  • your finger
